_metadata.independence: I read only u19-blind-input.json and no other file, repository content, web page or API.

hints.reason: A lion's mane is immediate, but nothing about a fish is a mane (the lion's mane jellyfish is not a fish and is a stretch anyway).
Fish live in the sea; sea lion is a familiar compound.
Contains both target words as substrings, which is a rule failure.

best_available.why: Fish in the sea plus sea lion reaches both sides plainly.

pairs.pair_note: SEA is the only servable hint; MANE is one-sided and LIONFISH breaks the substring rule.

hints.reason: Moon and night are inseparable, but fish only arrive via night fishing, which is a weak route.
Contains both target words as substrings; rule failure regardless of the real species.
The moon drives the tides clearly; fish reach tide only through tide pools and fishing the tide, which is recognizable but not firm.

best_available.why: Moon to tide is strong and tide sits in the fish's ocean world, so it is the only hint that gestures at both sides.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. TIDE is serviceable if the pair must be served; NIGHT is essentially a MOON-only hint.

hints.reason: Both are common household pets, a shared category any player sees.
Cats famously eat fish and chase mice; one shared scene reaches both.

best_available.why: The cartoon cat with a fish bone and a mouse hole is a single image that points at both targets.

pairs.pair_note: Both hints pass; CAT is the more vivid connection, PET the broader one.

hints.reason: Fish on Friday (fish fry Friday) is a familiar tradition and Friday night is a stock phrase.
Lanterns light the night clearly; the fish side rests on the lanternfish, a real but little-known species, or on lantern-lit night fishing.

best_available.why: Two everyday phrases, fish Friday and Friday night, meet in one word.

pairs.pair_note: FRIDAY is a clean PASS; LANTERN leans on the night side.

hints.reason: A school of fish is immediate, but nothing connects school to ocean on its own.
Fish live in the sea; sea is a near-synonym of ocean, which makes it very easy but still fair.
Finding Nemo stars a clownfish and its whole story is an ocean crossing; Captain Nemo adds a second ocean route.

best_available.why: A universally known fish character whose story is set in the ocean, without giving away a synonym.

pairs.pair_note: SEA passes but is nearly a synonym for OCEAN; NEMO is the richer hint. SCHOOL is FISH-only.

hints.reason: Fishing nets are immediate, but pirates have no recognizable net association beyond ship rigging.
Fish hook on one side, Captain Hook and the pirate hook hand on the other.
Fish swim the sea; pirates sail it.

best_available.why: Fish hook and the pirate's hook are both iconic and specific.

pairs.pair_note: Two good hints; NET only reaches FISH.

hints.reason: Triggerfish is a moderately known fish, but QUEEN is reachable only by knowing the queen triggerfish species, which a player will not supply.
Angelfish is a well-known fish; the queen side rests on the queen angelfish, a real reef species that only some players will know.
Fish and chips is immediate, but chips has no recognizable connection to queen.

best_available.why: The only hint with a real, if niche, route to QUEEN (queen angelfish) while reaching FISH clearly.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Both species-name hints need the specific 'queen X-fish' species to work; CHIPS is pure filler on the queen side.

hints.reason: Onion rings are immediate; fish only arrives via the fried-fish basket where onion rings are served alongside.
Calamari rings are the standard serving; calamari is squid, which sits in the seafood world next to fish but is not a fish.
Tuna is plainly a fish, but there is no tuna-to-ring route.

best_available.why: Calamari rings reach RING squarely and the seafood-menu context gets a player near FISH.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The ring side is well served by ring-shaped foods, but none is a fish; a true fish-ring link is missing.

hints.reason: Toy robots are classic; a toy fish (bath toy, wind-up fish) exists but is not a strong association.
A drone is a kind of robot, but there is no recognizable drone-to-fish route for a player.
Contains FISH as a substring (and Robo is a bare prefix of robot); rule failure.

best_available.why: Reaches ROBOT clearly and at least gestures at FISH through toy fish.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. This pair has little natural overlap; the toy-store route is the best available.

hints.reason: Contains both target words as substrings; rule failure.
Rock pool is a familiar compound (tide pool in US usage) and the small fish in it, plus fish ponds and fishing pools, reach the fish side.
Reef fish are the classic image; a reef is a ridge of rock.

best_available.why: A reef is rock teeming with fish; one scene, both words.

pairs.pair_note: REEF is a clean PASS; POOL is a fair PASS whose rock side is stronger for UK players.

hints.reason: Roses are pink; fish reach pink only through salmon flesh or the pink salmon, a colour route rather than a connection.
Salmon is plainly a fish; rose is reached only because salmon and rose are both pinkish shades.
Contains both target words as substrings; rule failure.

best_available.why: Rose to pink is firm and pink salmon gets a player to fish; the colour route is the only one this pair has.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The two colour hints mirror each other; neither reaches both words without leaning on pinkness.

hints.reason: Cured fish is a familiar food, and salt is the curing agent; one process reaches both.
Fish live in the sea; sea salt is an everyday compound.
Cod is a fish and salt cod is a well-known dish.

best_available.why: Broadest and most immediate on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: All three pass; a well-served pair.

hints.reason: Deep-sea fish and 'the deep' reach fish; deep shadow is a familiar modifier phrase, a shared-property route like SWEET for APPLE+HONEY.
Spooking a fish is angler jargon and spook-to-shadow needs a ghostly-figure explanation; neither side is reached clearly.

best_available.why: Reaches fish firmly and shadow through an ordinary phrase.

pairs.pair_note: DEEP is a modest PASS; SPOOK fails on both sides.

hints.reason: Sharks are the archetypal predator; fish only arrive because a shark is a predatory fish, which is a weak independent route.
Jaws is the shark film; fish is reached only because the title creature is a fish.
Fish fins and the shark fin cutting the surface are both immediate.

best_available.why: The one hint with a direct, independent route to each word.

pairs.pair_note: FIN passes; the other two are shark hints that reach fish only through the shark.

hints.reason: Both animals are covered in scales; a direct shared property.
Slippery fish is a stock image; snakes are slippery/slithering in common speech, a defensible shared property.
An eel is a fish that looks like a snake; the bridge creature between the two.

best_available.why: The most direct shared property, instantly true of both.

pairs.pair_note: All three pass; SLIPPERY is the softest.

hints.reason: Spider crab is a familiar compound; crab sits beside fish in the seafood/sea-creature world.
Spider web is immediate, but fishing nets are not called webs and fish has no web route.
Fishing net is immediate; a spider's web is net-like, but 'spider net' is not a phrase a player reaches for.

best_available.why: Spider crab gives a real compound and crab lives in the fish world.

pairs.pair_note: CRAB is a modest PASS; NET and WEB are mirror-image half-hints.

hints.reason: A salmon run is angler knowledge and the 'spring run' sense is jargon; spring is not reached from run on its own.
Fish swim in streams; a spring is the water source that feeds a stream.
Trout is plainly a fish; the spring side rests on spring creeks and trout season opening in spring, which is recognizable mostly to anglers.

best_available.why: Uses the water sense of spring and the natural home of fish.

pairs.pair_note: STREAM is a clean PASS; RUN and TROUT lean on fishing knowledge.

hints.reason: Pisces is the fish sign and a star sign/constellation.
Contains both target words as substrings; rule failure.
Patrick Star of SpongeBob gives star directly; fish is reached only through the undersea setting since Patrick is a starfish.

best_available.why: A familiar word whose meaning is literally the fish among the stars.

pairs.pair_note: PISCES passes cleanly; PATRICK is a fun but star-weighted hint.

hints.reason: Freight train is immediate; there is no recognizable freight-to-fish route.
Sardines are fish; 'packed like sardines' is the stock description of a crowded train carriage.

best_available.why: The only hint that reaches both, via the crowded-train idiom.

pairs.pair_note: SARDINES is a defensible PASS through a familiar idiom; FREIGHT is train-only.

hints.reason: Fresh fish and freshwater are both everyday compounds.
Fish swim; swimming happens in water.
Fish tank and water tank are both familiar compounds.

best_available.why: Two concrete compounds, no stretch on either side.

pairs.pair_note: All three pass; an easy pair.

hints.reason: Eye of newt in the witches' brew is immediate, but a newt is an amphibian with no recognizable fish route.
Ursula is the sea witch of The Little Mermaid, a story set among fish and half-fish characters; a shared-story route like POISON for APPLE+QUEEN.

best_available.why: The sea witch gives witch directly and the undersea story carries fish.

pairs.pair_note: URSULA is a story-route PASS; NEWT is witch-only.

hints.reason: Wolf pack is immediate; fish travel in schools, not packs, so there is no fish route.
Salmon is a fish; wolves do catch salmon in nature footage, but bears own that scene and the wolf link is secondary.
Contains both target words as substrings; rule failure.

best_available.why: The only hint that reaches wolf at all, through the river-hunting scene.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The pair lacks a natural shared scene beyond wolves fishing salmon.

hints.reason: Ghosts are see-through and glass is transparent; a direct shared property.
A mirror is glass, and the ghost in the mirror is a staple horror image.
Windows are glass; the ghostly face at the window is a recognizable haunted-house scene.

best_available.why: The defining shared property of both targets.

pairs.pair_note: All three pass; WINDOW is the softest on the ghost side.

hints.reason: Gold rush is immediate; ghost is reachable only via the explanation that ghost towns followed gold rushes.
Ghost town is immediate; gold arrives through the abandoned mining town, a real but secondary association.
Pirate gold is a stock phrase and ghost pirates (cursed crews, ghost ships) are a familiar trope.

best_available.why: Pirate gold and the ghost pirate reach both targets directly.

pairs.pair_note: PIRATE is the clean PASS; TOWN is a fair second choice; RUSH is gold-only.

hints.reason: Ghosts haunt; there is no recognizable haunt-to-heart route.
A heart stops; the ghost side needs the explanation that a fright stops your heart, which is not a ghost connection on its own.
Spirit is a synonym of ghost; heart is reached only through the 'heart and spirit' sense of inner feeling.

best_available.why: The only hint that touches heart at all while being certain on ghost.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The two words share little; the hints here are each essentially one-sided.

hints.reason: A veiled ghostly lady is a recognizable image and beekeepers wear veils, but neither side is reached clearly without explanation.
Honey trap is a familiar phrase and the ghost trap is the Ghostbusters device.
Ghosts say boo; boo is also a term of endearment like honey.

best_available.why: The ghost's own word doubling as a pet name is a neat two-way hit.

pairs.pair_note: BOO and TRAP both pass; VEIL needs two explanations.

hints.reason: Ice is cold and a ghost brings a cold spot or chill; a shared property.
A ghostly chill and ice chilling a drink both reach their targets; same route as COLD.
The Shining is a ghost story; ice arrives only via the frozen ending or shining ice, a secondary route.

best_available.why: Broadest shared property.

pairs.pair_note: COLD and CHILL are interchangeable passes; SHINING is a story route that half-works.

hints.reason: Ghostly cold is firm; 'cold iron' is a known phrase and iron is cold to the touch.
Ghosts rattle chains; chains are iron.
Haunted castle is immediate, but castle has no recognizable iron route.

best_available.why: The rattling iron chain is the ghost's own prop.

pairs.pair_note: CHAIN is excellent; COLD is a fair PASS; CASTLE is ghost-only.

hints.reason: Elvis is the King; the ghost side rests on Graceland ghost legends and 'Elvis lives' sightings, which is a secondary association.
Mufasa is the lion king who returns as a ghost in the clouds.
The ghost of King Hamlet is the play's most famous scene.

best_available.why: A king whose ghost scene is universally known.

pairs.pair_note: Two strong story-route passes; ELVIS is king-weighted.

hints.reason: Simba is a lion; the ghost belongs to Mufasa, so Simba only reaches ghost as the one who sees it.
Mufasa is a lion who appears as a ghost.

best_available.why: The lion who is the ghost.

pairs.pair_note: MUFASA is the right character; SIMBA is the witness, not the ghost.

hints.reason: Howling at the moon is a stock image; ghosts howl and wail in haunted-house lore.
Ghosts haunt; moon has no haunt route.
Moonwalk is a familiar compound and a ghost walk is a familiar tour/phrase for where ghosts walk at night.

best_available.why: Two real compounds, moonwalk and ghost walk.

pairs.pair_note: WALK and HOWL pass; HAUNT is ghost-only.

hints.reason: Mice squeak; ghost is reached only via squeaky floorboards, which is not a ghost connection.
Quiet as a mouse is idiomatic; ghosts move in silence, a defensible shared property.
Haunted is pure ghost; nothing about a mouse is haunted.

best_available.why: The only hint that reaches both, through the shared silence.

pairs.pair_note: QUIET is a soft PASS; the other two are each entirely one-sided.

hints.reason: 'Things that go bump in the night' names ghosts and night in one familiar phrase.
Ghosts haunt; night is reached only as the time hauntings happen.
Contains NIGHT as a substring; rule failure.

best_available.why: A single idiom that carries both words.

pairs.pair_note: BUMP is a clean PASS; MIDNIGHT breaks the substring rule.

hints.reason: The Flying Dutchman is the archetypal ghost ship doomed to sail the oceans.
The Titanic is the ocean liner; ghost arrives only via wreck ghost stories, a secondary route.
Ghost ship is a stock phrase and ships sail the ocean.

best_available.why: Broadest two-way compound.

pairs.pair_note: SHIP and DUTCHMAN pass; TITANIC is ocean-weighted.

hints.reason: Cursed pirates (the Black Pearl crew) are familiar; a cursed spirit is a common ghost framing.
Pirates of the Caribbean is immediate; ghost arrives only via the film's undead crew, which needs explaining.
Ghost ship and pirate ship are both stock compounds.

best_available.why: Both targets form a stock compound with ship.

pairs.pair_note: SHIP is excellent; CURSED a fair PASS; CARIBBEAN is pirate-weighted.

hints.reason: Bohemian Rhapsody by Queen is immediate; there is no ghost route.
The headless ghost (Headless Horseman) is firm; queen is reached only by recalling a beheaded queen such as Anne Boleyn.
Queen Anne and Anne Boleyn make queen reachable; the ghost side is the Anne Boleyn haunting legend, which fewer players know.

best_available.why: Firm on ghost and the beheaded-queen route is at least a famous story.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. HEADLESS and ANNE both rely on the same Anne Boleyn legend from opposite ends; BOHEMIAN is queen-only.

hints.reason: Both sides depend on the film The Ring, where the ghost girl comes from a well; without the film, well reaches neither word.
Ring a bell is immediate; a tolling bell is not a recognizable ghost route.
Samara is the ghost of The Ring; the connection is exact on both sides for anyone who knows the film, though the name is less known than the film.

best_available.why: Exact two-way hit for players who know the film, which is the only route this pair has.

pairs.pair_note: SAMARA passes on exactness despite niche recognizability; WELL is the same film route from a vaguer word.

hints.reason: A robot is a machine; 'ghost in the machine' is a familiar phrase.
Pac-Man's ghosts are immediate, but Pac-Man is not a robot and has no robot route.
Ghost in the Shell is a well-known cyborg/robot title; a robot's shell is also its casing.

best_available.why: Robot is a machine and the ghost phrase is widely known.

pairs.pair_note: MACHINE and SHELL both pass via famous phrases; PACMAN is ghost-only.

hints.reason: Haunted is pure ghost; rock has no haunted route.
Ghosts rise from the graveyard; a gravestone is a slab of rock.
Same route as GRAVESTONE: the ghost's graveyard marker is a stone.

best_available.why: The graveyard stone reaches both words; TOMBSTONE is marginally the more iconic spelling.

pairs.pair_note: Two interchangeable passes; HAUNTED is ghost-only.
